subject: Post-call: air-gapped on-prem requirements, patch cadence & spare parts
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Arya Patel <arya.patel@biosynth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: air-gapped on-prem requirements, patch cadence & spare parts

Thanks again for the call earlier today — appreciate the clear context on BioSynth’s constraints. Below is a short recap and concrete next steps so we can align logistics for a Private (air-gapped) deployment.

Recap (what we heard)
- You are targeting an air-gapped, on-prem appliance in the Stanford data center (no outbound internet from the inference cluster).
- Primary workloads: inference for internal R&D (low-latency batch, bursty) and a small external QA sandbox.
- Desired SLA window for maintenance: maintenance windows only during a monthly 2-hour off-peak slot (Saturdays 02:00–04:00 local).
- No persistent remote admin access; remote console only via customer-controlled jumpbox during scheduled windows.

Immediate asks for sizing & ops planning
1) Hardware inventory: can you share current rack, power per-cabinet, and on-site contact for the DC ops team? (I attached a short site-survey template).
2) Spare parts: we recommend a minimum of 2 spare NVMe modules + 1 spare PSU per appliance. Please confirm procurement timelines.
3) Upgrade policy: you asked about offline upgrades and rollback — we have a documented Maintenance & Offline Upgrade MOP; it supports image-based upgrades with a local rollback image and requires a one-hour slot for typical patch + validation.

Proposed next steps
- BioSynth: send the completed site-survey and confirm DC contact by 2026-11-06.
- Redwood: we'll share the MOP, a spare-parts checklist, and a sample SOW for air-gapped installs.
- Schedule: propose a site survey week of 2026-11-15, followed by a pilot install window in early December.

Attachments: site-survey-template.xlsx (please fill & return)

Thanks — I’ll loop Diego for the runbook details once we have the survey.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0189
From: Arya Patel <arya.patel@biosynth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops+infra@biosynth.com
Date: 2026-11-03T09:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: air-gapped on-prem requirements, patch cadence & spare parts

Thanks, Soojin — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Inventory: attaching an initial rack diagram in the next email (ops team is compiling). We have single-circuit PDUs in the rack; can Redwood support N+1 PSU configuration?
2) Spare parts procurement: procurement lead says standard lead times are 6–8 weeks, but we can prioritize NVMe spares if needed.
3) Remote support: we cannot allow vendor-initiated outbound SSH. If there is an emergency we will provide time-limited access through our jumpbox; remote console over serial-over-LAN is acceptable when initiated from our side.
4) Upgrade rollback: what level of data loss (if any) should we plan for during rollback? Is the rollback node an image we keep on a separate encrypted drive?

Also — we will need the SOW and a high-level cost estimate before our procurement commit. Can you flag anything that would be out of scope for Redwood in an air-gapped install (e.g., on-site labor, rack/power cabling)?

Regards,
Arya
Infrastructure Manager, BioSynth Therapeutics
arya.patel@biosynth.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Arya Patel <arya.patel@biosynth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T11:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: air-gapped on-prem requirements, patch cadence & spare parts

Hi Arya — good questions, answered inline below.

1) PSU / N+1: our appliances support dual-redundant PSUs; we recommend N+1 at the rack-level for critical workloads. Redwood can supply redundant PSUs as part of the hardware BOM, we just need confirmation on rack PDU circuits so we size PDUs accordingly.

2) Spare parts procurement: NVMe and PSUs on the spare checklist are the only parts I’d classify as mission-critical for a 99.9% uptime target. If lead times are long, plan to pre-order these separately and keep them on-site. See spare-parts-checklist.csv attached.

3) Remote support constraints: understood and acceptable — our standard air-gap playbook follows the customer-controlled jumpbox model. All support sessions are initiated by your team and logged; we do not initiate outbound access.

4) Upgrade rollback and data risk: rollback uses a pre-staged encrypted disk image stored on a removable drive (we recommend a second drive kept in a different locked cabinet). Typical stateful model cache is re-built from KV snapshots; there is a non-zero but small window of model-cache warm-up — no persistent customer data is altered during the process; still, we recommend a verification run post-rollback. I’ve attached the Redwood_MOP_offline_upgrade_v1.pdf with the step-by-step sequence and estimated timings (page 3 has rollback plan).

Out-of-scope (to call out for SOW)
- On-site rack & cabling labor (we can include via partner but costed separately)
- Data center cross-connect procurement (customer responsibility)
- Long-term spare-parts inventory (we can offer procurement as a managed service for an additional fee)

Next steps (updated)
- BioSynth: return the site-survey + confirm DC ops contact by 2026-11-06.
- Redwood: attach MOP and spare checklist (done), prepare draft SOW + pricing and share by 2026-11-05.

Attachments: Redwood_MOP_offline_upgrade_v1.pdf, spare-parts-checklist.csv

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: pricing and support model options for BioSynth

Internal note — pulling together options to present in the SOW:

1) Air-gapped install SOW (baseline): appliance + on-site commissioning (partner labor) + 12 months of remote monitoring (events only; no remote access).
2) Managed spares add-on: one-time procurement + 12 months of storage & rotation (pricing in attached draft).
3) Alternative: Dedicated capacity (hosted within Redwood-managed colo) could obviate the air-gap constraints for BioSynth but requires acceptance of off-site managed model data flow — pricing estimate attached (dedicated-pricing-estimate.pdf).

Notes for SOW: include explicit clause for customer-initiated access windows, clarifying jumpbox control and audit logging. Also include firmware-patch cadence (quarterly) with emergency patches allowed outside window only with written approval.

I’ll hand the draft SOW to Legal once we have the completed site survey.

—
Neha Kapoor
Director, Solutions & Technical Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Arya Patel <arya.patel@biosynth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops+infra@biosynth.com
Date: 2026-11-06T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: air-gapped on-prem requirements, patch cadence & spare parts

Thanks all — this is helpful. We’ll do the following:
- Site survey will be completed and returned by EOD 2026-11-09.
- Procurement will prioritize NVMe spares and confirm lead times; expect PO request by 2026-11-20 if pricing matches SOW.
- We accept the customer-initiated jumpbox model and the proposed rollback approach; please include the verification checklist in the SOW.

Request: can Redwood provide a draft SOW and an initial PO-ready quote by COB 2026-11-05? We’d like to get procurement moving. If you can also include a suggested date for a 2-hour pilot upgrade window in early December, that would help us reserve the DC slot.

If that works, I’ll loop in procurement next week.

Regards,
Arya
